solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dull book hack put out

indicators.note: something put out is ejected, so the hacking word is thrown out of the book's name

parts.note: a Gospel, a book of the New Testament
to hack is to chop or hew

explanation.surface: A dreary book from a hack writer gets published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book hack' reads as a hack writer, but book is the Gospel of Matthew and hack is the verb, removed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Matt describes a surface or colour lacking shine or lustre.

clue.text: NZ insect, a yellow one joining bee in cup

indicators.note: in says everything before it sits inside the drinking vessel
joining says the next piece is placed alongside what comes before

parts.note: first part of a mug, a cup
or is gold or yellow in heraldry

explanation.surface: A New Zealand insect falls into a cup beside a bee.
explanation.walkthrough: The cup is split open to hold everything else. Or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori bug is a large wingless cockroach native to New Zealand.

clue.text: A blast comes from one President needing a change of heart

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter, and changing it swaps that letter for another

explanation.surface: A president is blasted for flip-flopping.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUMP has its central U changed to O. A tromp is an old word for a trumpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tromp is an archaic trumpet, the instrument a fanfare blast issues from.

clue.text: Abnormal awareness of a lie — the asset seen as extraordinary

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone senses a lie behind an asset's value.
explanation.definitionFit: Telaesthesia is perception of distant events beyond the normal senses, a paranormal kind of perception.

clue.text: European region in which to get intradermal sedative

indicators.note: the region is where the next item is got, so it holds that abbreviation

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Europe a sedative is given by injection into the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: ID, the abbreviation for intradermal, goes inside THRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thridace is inspissated lettuce juice, once used medicinally as a calming drug.

clue.text: A god rising in the earth, what?

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A puzzled bystander sees a god emerging from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces together are read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Helios is the Greek sun deity who drives his chariot across the sky.

clue.text: Let a group of children talk

indicators.note: a group of letters is picked out of the following words

explanation.surface: A request to let some kids speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A let is a property leased to a tenant, which is a rental.

clue.text: Awfully thin ladies keeping off booze, affecting to be arty

indicators.note: awfully means very badly, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Skinny women on the wagon pose as art lovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeping' looks like a container signal, but 'keeping off booze' is the whole phrase for teetotal, TT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante dabbles in the arts superficially, so dilettantish behaviour is a pose of artistic taste.

clue.text: Bill appearing in Syrian cloth made from plant fibre

indicators.note: appearing in means sitting inside the cloth word

parts.note: a woven fabric of goat or camel hair from Syria

explanation.surface: A bill turns up for Syrian fabric woven from plant fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: Aba is a Middle Eastern woven fabric; 'made from' links the definition, which is only 'plant fibre'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaca is Manila hemp, the strong fibre from a Philippine banana relative.

clue.text: Senility of dishonourable man descending on university — Oxford maybe

indicators.note: in a down entry, descending on puts the first part above what follows

parts.note: Oxford is an example of a city

explanation.surface: A disgraced old don's decline at an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Caducity means the frailty and decay of old age, a falling away.

clue.text: Financial allowances for divorcees?

explanation.surface: A question about alimony paid to former partners.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for expense money and also the plural of ex, a former husband or wife.

clue.text: React furiously about money paid for units under flood?

indicators.note: about means surrounding the payment word
acting furiously means wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone reacts angrily to a charge for flood damage.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled ACRET goes round FEE.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre-foot is a measure of water volume, the amount covering one acre to a depth of one foot.

clue.text: Old distiller making money in Greece once

explanation.surface: A veteran distiller earns a fortune in ancient Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: Bols is a Dutch firm famous for gin and liqueurs.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greek currency.

clue.text: Divine Scottish area about to be sealed off

indicators.note: sealed off means shut out, so that letter is removed

explanation.surface: A Scottish region about to be cordoned off.
explanation.walkthrough: C for circa is taken out of SPACE. Divine is a verb here: to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: Spae is a Scots verb meaning to foretell or prophesy, as a seer does.

clue.text: Group in small valley

explanation.surface: A band performing in a little valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Slade were a British glam-rock band famous for 'Merry Xmas Everybody'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a famous English rock band and also a dialect word for a glade or little dell.

clue.text: Primate organised Eucharist, having introduced plan

indicators.note: introduced means put inside, so the other word goes into the rearranged letters
organised means put in a new order, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A bishop arranges a Mass with a plan in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like a church leader, which suits the Eucharist; it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramapithecus is a fossil ape genus from the Miocene, once thought an ancestor of humans.

clue.text: Optical problem puts wolf into unconscious state

indicators.note: puts into means places inside the other word

parts.note: a timber wolf of the western US

explanation.surface: An eye condition that a wolf knocks out cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Lobo is a Spanish-derived name for the grey or timber wolf of the American West.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloboma is a gap or defect in a structure of the eye such as the iris.

clue.text: Architectural feature within elegant atrium

indicators.note: within means found inside the following words

explanation.surface: A feature in a stylish entrance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: An anta is a pilaster at the end of a side wall in classical buildings.

clue.text: Class prejudice? Sect aims to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: A religious group sets out to end snobbery.
explanation.definitionFit: Casteism is discrimination based on hereditary social rank, a bias rooted in social stratification.

clue.text: Leaders are excessively preoccupied, cycling round after setback

indicators.note: a setback sends things backwards, so the word is read in reverse
cycling round moves letters from one end to the other in a loop

explanation.surface: Managers fret obsessively about recovering from a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: OBSESS reads SSESBO backwards; cycling the last two letters to the front gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosses are those in charge, the heads of an organisation.

clue.text: Country pillar beside the Roman way

indicators.note: beside says the two parts are set next to each other

parts.note: a lat is an Indian monolithic pillar

explanation.surface: A column stands by an ancient Roman road through the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Latvia is a Baltic state in north-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Governor heading off across street in coat

indicators.note: lying across something means spanning it, so it goes around
heading off means losing the head, the first letter

explanation.surface: A governor sets off across the road in an overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In coat' looks like a container signal, but 'coat' is the definition and 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulster is a long loose overcoat, originally of Irish frieze.

clue.text: Russia's No 1 female tennis player makes return

explanation.surface: A top Russian woman returns serve on court.
explanation.definitionFit: To revert is to go back to an earlier state, to come back.

clue.text: Identity given to workers — they were deemed to be in cells

definitions.text: they were deemed to be in cells

explanation.surface: Staff are issued ID that is checked against prison inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Idants were the hypothetical hereditary units Weismann supposed existed in the chromatin of cells.

clue.text: Fish? One Indian snake eats any number

indicators.note: something that eats takes in, so the snake word holds the number

parts.note: a naga is a cobra or serpent deity in India
n is any number in maths

explanation.surface: An Indian snake swallowing countless fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The query marks the definition as a category guess: the inanga is a small New Zealand fish whose young are whitebait.
explanation.definitionFit: Inanga is a small New Zealand galaxiid fish, caught as whitebait when young.

clue.text: Disease of sheep getting dingy over time

indicators.note: in a down entry, over puts the first part above what follows

explanation.surface: Sheep look grubby as illness lingers over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunt is a Scots name for a sheep disease, a form of gid causing staggering.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about hard butter

indicators.note: about means going round the other letter

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed at how firm the butter is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghee is clarified butter used widely in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Habit of one elevated as fool holding America up

indicators.note: holding means gripping the other word inside
in a down entry, up means read from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A monk's robe on someone promoted makes him look a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit means clothing, not a custom; the one elevated is a pilot. Git is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A G-suit is pressurised clothing worn by airmen flying high to resist acceleration forces.

clue.text: Prospect of saint in the middle of life

indicators.note: in the middle of means placed centrally inside the other word

explanation.surface: A holy person's outlook in midlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a wide view of scenery, a long view.

clue.text: Franciscan old boy, one labouring in East

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy friar works in the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The Observantines were the branch of Franciscan friars keeping the strict rule of the order.

clue.text: Poem's found to be offensive, not half, by Catholic

definitions.note: possessive standing for an adjective: of a poem

indicators.note: by in its sense of alongside or next to, so the second part follows directly
not half means only half the word is kept

explanation.surface: A poem by a Catholic is judged rather offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: ODIOUS loses its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Odic means relating to an ode, a lyric poem, so it stands for the possessive.

clue.text: Don't hesitate to employ a heavy blow

explanation.surface: An urging to strike hard without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an instruction: 'do use' a heavy blow.
explanation.definitionFit: Douse is an old word for a hard punch or strike, as in 'dowse'.

clue.text: Time is given to religious instruction in part of Jewish calendar

explanation.surface: Religion lessons are scheduled at a Jewish season.
explanation.walkthrough: RI is religious instruction, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisri is the first month of the Jewish civil year, usually falling in September or October.

clue.text: Wind rages furiously across estuary

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the scrambled letters go around the abbreviation
furiously means wildly, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A gale rages fiercely over a river mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Argestes was the classical name for the north-west wind.

clue.text: Places of torture using whips when army moves in

indicators.note: something that moves in goes inside the other word

explanation.surface: Soldiers arrive at torture chambers where whips are used.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force; cat-o'-nine-tails whips are cats.
explanation.definitionFit: A catasta was a scaffold or stage used for torture or for exhibiting slaves.

clue.text: Straw left in meat

indicators.note: in means placed inside the food word

explanation.surface: Straw left inside a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Halm, or haulm, is the stalks and stems of crops, i.e. straw.
